name: Wall push-up
why: Pushing strength helps you punch the ball clear. It also helps you get up fast after a dive.

setup.space: Floor reaching about an arm and a half from a solid wall.

steps: Face the wall, hands on it at shoulder height. Place them a little wider than your shoulders.
Walk your feet back until your body leans in one straight line.
Bend the elbows to bring your chest toward the wall. Keep the elbows angled back.
Push the wall away until your arms are straight.

mistakes.fix: Squeeze the bottom so the body stays straight.
Angle the elbows back, halfway between the body and straight out.
Tuck the chin a little and let the chest lead.

parent_check: Straight line from head to heels
stop_if: Pain in the shoulder, elbow or wrist
Pain that changes how you move
Chest pain, a racing heartbeat or unusual shortness of breath
Feet slipping on the floor (fix the footing before going on)

easier.use_when: The body sags or the reps slow down.

harder.variant: Hands on a stable step or the bottom stair, feet further back.
harder.move_on_when: Every rep clean two sessions in a row, and the owner approves.

dose.tempo: down for two, push away smoothly
